chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) regarding:

Regarding a man who prayed Dhuhr in the Mosque of the Tree, and contracted the Ihram, then touched perfume or hunted game or had intercourse with his wife, he said: There is no penalty upon him as long as he has not said the Talbiyah.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: The ritual declaration of intent and praise of God during Hajj
key_terms.صَيْد: Game or wild animals hunted by the pilgrim
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الشَّجَرَةِ: The Mosque of the Tree, a specific location in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for breaking Ihram before reciting the Talbiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain clarifies that the binding legal consequences of Ihram, such as financial compensation (daman) for hunting or marital relations, are contingent upon the formal declaration via the Talbiyah rather than mere entry into the Miqat. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the verbal intent (niyyah) and declaration as the pivotal moment for incurring obligations, distinguishing it from the physical state of being in the sacred boundary.
